body:
## Summary

- Verified live against current `dev`: `internal/device/registry.go`'s `Registry` has no cross-device pairing at all -- a configured device that never matches syslog traffic just sits at `EventCount == 0` forever, and the real traffic auto-discovers as a separate, unconfigured entry (`ID: sourceIP`) with no link back to the declared one. `internal/routerstate.go` and `internal/naming.go` have no related logic either (grepped for `sourceIp`/`SourceIp` across `internal/`). The defect issue #442 describes is live.
- Added `Registry.MultihomedCandidates()`: pairs every configured device with zero events under its own identity with every currently auto-discovered (undeclared) device. This is evidence assembly only -- Registry has no way to know *which* discovered device (if any) is the same physical router as a given silent declared one, so it reports every live candidate rather than guessing at one (same "several rules share a prefix, report all of them" honesty rule `RulesForLogPrefix` already follows).
- Added the docs paragraph #442 asked for in `routeros-setup.md`'s push section (4b): the token's device must equal the event's `deviceId`, and a multi-homed router's source address is the usual reason it doesn't.

## What this PR deliberately does not do

#442 also asks for this to surface through a wizard step and/or a "systems analysis / topography surface", with owner-drafted example wording for the wizard case. Per the issue itself, both of those are **not built yet**: the wizard rework is v0.3.0 phase 2 (the parent epic, #385, hasn't reached it), and the analysis surface is described as "whatever standing analysis view we build" -- it doesn't exist. Both are also outside this task's scope (`internal/api/`, `main.go`, and frontend `src/` are excluded here).

More importantly, per `AGENTS.md`'s freshly-added "UX and UI design is Fable 5's work" section: "wording what the interface tells the operator" is design, not implementation, here. Even though the owner drafted example copy in the issue body, *where* this evidence surfaces (wizard step vs. analysis view, or both), how it reads alongside the wizard's other checks, and the final interface wording are still open judgement calls -- the issue itself offers the two placements as alternatives without deciding between them. I'm stopping short of that and handing back `MultihomedCandidates()` as the evidence primitive a Fable-designed surface (or a follow-up ticket) can build on.

## Fail-first proof

`internal/device/registry_test.go`'s four new tests reference `Registry.MultihomedCandidates()`, which didn't exist before this change. Reverted just `internal/device/registry.go` via a patch (`git diff > patch; git apply -R patch`) and reran the new tests: build failure, `r.MultihomedCandidates undefined (type *Registry has no field or method MultihomedCandidates)`, for all four. Reapplied the patch and reran: all four pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')` -- empty
- [x] `go vet ./...` -- clean
- [x] `go test ./...` -- all packages pass
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/device/...` -- pass
- [x] Fail-first proof on all 4 new tests (see above)
- Not run: `make live-check` -- this change touches neither the server, the UI, nor the CLI (pure `internal/device` package + a docs paragraph)

Part of #442 (does not close it)

---

**Scope correction (orchestrator, not the author):** the `Closes #442` this PR opened with has been removed. #442's own body scopes the operator-facing half to the wizard rework — *"the wizard is replaced surface (phase 2), so this is scoped there, not built standalone"* — and this PR deliberately and correctly stops at the evidence primitive plus the docs paragraph. Closing the issue here would have marked the explaining half done when it is not. The surfacing is tracked on #487 (wizard modal).
title: Detect declared-but-silent devices alongside undeclared traffic (#442)
